scope: Visual direction previews before frontend implementation

prompts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a beautifully art-directed, high fidelity flat desktop web application mockup for "SatQuery AI", an ISRO-problem student prototype for satellite image analysis through natural-language questions. Landscape 16:10, approximately 1600x1000, sharp legible typography, screenshot of the actual application filling the entire frame, no laptop/device frame, no perspective, no surroundings. This is an operating application, not a landing page. All text spelled correctly; limit copy to the exact short labels below. Satellite landscape is generated illustrative imagery, not a real measured dataset. Show persistent small label "Design preview · Illustrative data". Brand uses a small elegant orbital line symbol and SatQuery AI wordmark. User task: upload one/two GeoTIFFs, ask a question, compare satellite scenes, inspect an answer and visible execution receipt. Core mode tabs "Single image", "Change detection", "Optical + SAR". Visible upload action "Add scenes". Query text "What changed along the river?" Clear "Ask SatQuery" action. No invented numerical accuracy, no confidence percentages, no live badge, no customer claims. Result section must say "Illustrative result" and "Possible water expansion near the eastern bank." Receipt has stages "Check inputs", "Choose tool", "Inspect evidence", plus note "Analysis tools are currently stubs." Clearly designed icon system, generous but precise spacing, exquisite hierarchy, thin rules, strong accessible contrast. Avoid purple gradients, sci-fi holograms, gratuitous dashboard statistics, generic equal-card grids. Draw a convincing lush satellite aerial river meander through green and ochre agricultural fields, not a generic globe. DIRECTION A: SCENE DESK. A confident, warm-black cartographic worktable. Dominant 68% left satellite viewport with a narrow 64px vertical tool rail on its far left, refined charcoal top header, and a stationary right 28% inspection drawer in deep forest-black. The entire image viewer forms one quiet canvas with rich detailed aerial imagery; a thin amber divider with draggable handle reveals BEFORE vs AFTER with discrete date chips "12 Jun 2024" / "24 Jun 2024". Subtle amber hatched evidence outline near eastern riverbank; map zoom controls and small scale "Illustrative scale". Small scene strip with two thumbnails along bottom left of image. Right drawer: heading "River corridor"; mode tabs; question in a spacious warm-grey input field; large restrained amber Ask SatQuery button. Beneath, compact answer and open execution receipt in a ruled vertical list. At footer of drawer one quiet "Export receipt" text button. Typography like refined IBM Plex Sans; mono reserved for dates/coordinates. Paper-white text, desaturated warm secondary text, golden ochre #e6ae59 actions. Map occupies the first visual attention, no gigantic heading. Title "Scene Desk" is not page content: product brand only. Everything feels like an exceptional professional image editor designed for earth observation. Receipt stage subtitles must name real stages "Checker", "Router", "Tool"; visible "Tool: stub". Controls include "Confidence: not measured" and "Download JSON".

A narrow shared scrubber/date track immediately below.
